events.content:
Done. The category links now navigate instantly with no loading state, and the URLs are unchanged (`/catalog?category=featured`, `/catalog?category=sale`).

**What was wrong:** `app/catalog/page.tsx` awaited `searchParams` on the server, which made the page dynamic under `cacheComponents`. Link prefetch could only fetch the static shell up to the Suspense boundary, so every click hit the server, waited on the 800ms `getProducts` call, and showed "Loading category..." in the meantime.

**What changed:**

- `lib/data.ts` — `getProducts` now has a `'use cache'` directive, so its results are cacheable and prerenderable instead of forcing a runtime render.
- `app/catalog/page.tsx` — the server page no longer reads `searchParams`. It fetches the products for every known category from the cache and passes the whole map to a client component. With no dynamic API access, the page prerenders as fully static, so Link prefetch delivers all category data before the click.
- `app/catalog/category-results.tsx` (new client component) — reads `?category=` with `useSearchParams()` and picks the matching heading ("Products on sale" vs "Featured products") and product list from the prepared map. On client-side navigation the search params are available synchronously, so the Suspense fallback never shows.
- `lib/categories.ts` (new) — the category list, shared by the home page and the catalog page so the prepared categories always match the rendered links. `app/page.tsx` now imports it; its `/catalog?category=...` hrefs are untouched.

**Verified:** `next build` reports `/catalog` as `○ (Static)`; the prerendered page embeds all four products from both categories; and both the RSC prefetch request and a direct page request return in ~5ms against the production server — no 800ms render on click. The build also auto-adjusted `tsconfig.json` (`jsx: react-jsx` plus an include entry), which is Next's standard mandatory change.

One trade-off to be aware of: the page now ships every category's products to the client and revalidates on the cache's schedule (15m default), which is the right shape here with two small categories — if the catalog grows large, you'd switch to per-category cached fetches instead of one combined map.
